summary: Join our training course on digital payments in social protection programs. Learn to implement effective solutions that improve efficiency and accessibility.
lede: Digital payments in social protection programs are electronic transfers of cash benefits to eligible households. This course is for intermediate professionals who manage benefit delivery or support its payment, identity, data, and oversight functions, and helps them assess how transfers reach recipients. Participants practice measuring payment performance, comparing payment service providers, and designing reconciliation and grievance workflows.
audienceIntro: This course suits professionals who manage the end-to-end delivery of cash benefits or support the payment, identity, data, protection, and oversight functions that make transfers work. It is appropriate for intermediate professionals who have operational exposure to social protection, payments, financial inclusion, or public-service delivery.
prerequisites: You should have practical exposure to social protection delivery, cash transfer operations, payment services, financial inclusion, public finance, identity management, monitoring and evaluation, or related program functions. No programming is required. Basic spreadsheet skills help with the payment data exercises, and you should bring a laptop with spreadsheet software. Advanced subjects such as AI-assisted anomaly detection, ISO 20022 messaging, digital identity architecture, and interoperability are taught at conceptual and operational application levels, not production engineering level.
